curated.tagline: No-account iPhone remote for an electric scooter, over Bluetooth LE
curated.description: A lightweight Swift/SwiftUI app that talks to a HopCycle W3 Max electric scooter directly over Bluetooth LE: a native port of the Voltix FF60 protocol recovered from the vendor's Android app. No backend, no cloud, no account. Private repository.
highlights: BLE protocol recovered from the vendor's Android app: service UUIDs, frame layout, CRC-16
Live dashboard (speed, battery, fault code), lock, lights, gear, speed limit, cruise control
Unbind, reset and OTA commands deliberately not implemented
No backend, no cloud, no account binding
curated.architecture: SwiftUI → CoreBluetooth → scooter BLE service FF60 (notify and write characteristics)

showcase.whatItIs: An iPhone remote for a HopCycle W3 Max electric scooter that talks to it directly over Bluetooth LE, with no backend, cloud or account.
showcase.whoItsFor: Owners of a HopCycle W3 Max who want control without binding to the vendor's cloud account.
showcase.whatLukeBuilt: A native Swift/SwiftUI port of the Voltix FF60 BLE protocol, decoded from the vendor's Android app: scan and connect, a live dashboard, lock and unlock, lights, gear, speed limit and cruise control. Unbind, reset and OTA commands are deliberately left out so the app cannot brick the scooter.
showcase.status: Working client. UUIDs, frame layout and CRC are high confidence; telemetry decoding is provisional until checked against the scooter's display.
